newsitem.title: BAHAMAS: Bahamas mops up as Lili races through Atlantic.
newsitem.headline: Bahamas mops up as Lili races through Atlantic.

text.p: The Bahamas on Monday assessed damage to islands hardest hit by Hurricane Lili as the weakened storm raced through the open Atlantic.

Lili's 90 mph (145 kph) winds ripped off roofs, damaged resort hotels and flattened banana plantations in the central Bahamas, particularly Long Island, Exuma and San Salvador, but no casualties were reported, government spokesman Chris Symmonett said.

At 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT) on Monday Lili's centre was at latitude 34.2 north, longitude 57.2 west, about 450 miles (725 km) east-northeast of Bermuda and moving northeast at 18 mph (30 kph), the National Hurricane Centre in Miami said.
Maximum sustained winds had decreased to 75 mph (120 kph) and the storm was expected to weaken slowly in coming days, forecasters said.

Lili bypassed Bermuda on Sunday, sparing the British colony the worst of its winds and rain, after a rampage that began last week off the coast of Central America. Flooding from the storm was blamed for 10 deaths in Nicaragua, Honduras and Costa Rica before it moved north over Cuba and then east through the central Bahamas.
The Bahamian government said on Monday it would likely announce a relief effort to islands in the central Bahamas later this week.
Lili also did considerable damage to the banana crop on Long Island, forcing the government to consider at least partially lifting a ban on imported bananas.
